content.thinking:
I'm planning out the fox's design in one pass without testing first—a standing pose facing forward, cream white coat with red and gold markings, nine fanned tails tipped in blue-gold flame, and now working through the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hip root and spine chain.

Building the spine and neck chains...

Still placing body stations...

Continuing the top of the chain near the neck, then I'm setting up the fur material: a cel-shaded cream coat with a slightly darker furry edge pattern for texture.

Now I'm working out the leg rigs — defining shoulder, hip, and foot positions for the front and hind legs, then figuring out segment lengths and joint bend directions to get a digitigrade stance with three-segment limbs.

I'm naming the joint chains per side (left/right) and attaching them to the appropriate spine or hip parent joints.

Now I'm defining tapered leg radii and applying a cream-to-red gradient paint shaded with cel shading, reusing this same leg material for both sides.

I'm shaping the paw as a small flattened ellipsoid at each foot tip, then adding three gold claw spikes spread across each paw using the spike primitive.

For the head, I'm placing a scaled sphere for the skull and building a tapered frustum box for the muzzle, anchored relative to the head joint's forward and down directions.

For the snout I'm using a rounded sweep for a softer fox-like shape, adding a jaw joint parented to the head with its own sweep and cream coloring, plus a dark sphere for the nose tip and amber decal eyes with facial markings.

For the eye decals I'm positioning them on the skull surface around the head center, mirroring placement for left versus right, and tilting each eye's roll outward so the outer corners lift slightly, giving that classic slanted fox-eye look.

Now I'm working out ear placement as triangular extrusions set above and to the side of the head center, defining their outline shape in local coordinates so they mirror correctly for left and right.

I notice the face normal flips for the mirrored side, so I need to handle the inner ear shape differently depending on orientation—making the red inner ear slightly thicker so it pokes through both faces rather than relying on a consistent normal direction.

Now I'm thinking about adding cheek fur and a neck ruff using cream-tinted tuft cards scattered over the body surface, filtered by height, with a simple pointed leaf-shaped SVG as the tuft texture.

For the collar, I'm considering a gold necklace made from a ring or loop of beads placed around the neck base joint.

Switching to decals instead of procedural markings seems easier—I'll place red swirl decals on the shoulders and haunches with a gold dot accent, mirroring them across sides as needed. Now I'm setting up the tail joints, planning for nine tails branching from a base near the rump.

Computing tail paths...

Still mapping tail curve points...

Still planning tail chain joints...

Placing the decal mark along the tail sweep, figuring out the orientation vectors so it projects correctly onto the tapering surface...

I'm placing roughly 18 decals in total (pairs at different angles along the tail), keeping the geometry cheap with 8x8 grids so the triangle count stays reasonable. Then I'm sketching flame shapes for the tips—blue and gold glowing cards to sit at the ends.

Writing flame card placement logic...

The tail chain tapers to zero radius at its tip where the flame begins. For floating spirit flames (hitodama), I'm planning small glowing orbs scattered around the body, attached to the hips bone so they move naturally, using flame-textured cards positioned at points like roughly ±0.7 and ±0.55 along the sides at varying heights, each with a small glowing core sphere.

I'm adding a flame card sized small for each orb, keeping them above floor level so nothing clips through. For the forehead, I'm placing a diamond-shaped decal marking using the skull's surface normal at a forward, upward angle. For cheek details, I'm scattering small fur-tuft cards across the skull surface, filtered to the cheek region away from center.

Then I'm scattering spiky cards along the neck top for a mane crest with a golden tint, followed by gold accents like a forehead crescent decal and a small gold-and-red pendant hanging at the chest, placed using a loop path along the body surface.

Adding small fang details...

Now I'm planning whiskers as thin rod geometry attached to the head bone, a few per side with a cream color, plus a tiny dark nose sphere at the muzzle tip. I'm also sizing the skull and overall body proportions to match a fox roughly 0.9 meters long.

Then I'm working through the muzzle and neck geometry — placing the eyes relative to skull radius, tracing a path from the head forward to the nose tip with tapering sweep radii, and reconciling the neck and head joint positions so the head sits high while the muzzle tilts slightly downward.

I'm now checking the body loft station near the head and confirming the spine/neck bone chains share overlapping path segments correctly, then working on hiding the tail root inside the rump by setting its starting point buried within the hip radius, and beginning to lay out the spine chain joint coordinates from the hips upward.

Writing joint coordinates...

Adding haunch and shoulder spheres for muscle bulk, then sweeping leg chains with tapered radii and ellipsoid paw shapes colored in cel-shaded red tones.

Now I'm defining the color palette (cream, red, gold, flame blue) and starting to write an SVG marking design with a swirl path.

Still writing SVG markup...

Drawing a simple fur tuft shape tinted cream white, then moving on to hitodama orbs and the component's structure—checking which imports I actually need like frame, rng, and catmull path utilities to avoid unused import errors.

Building out the kitsune rig: creating a builder instance, setting up the hips joint and spine chain using a catmull curve, and positioning the head joint relative to the neck with appropriate direction vectors.

Now I'm defining the jaw joint relative to the head using local-space offsets for position and aim, then working out the ear geometry with an extrusion that uses local offsets for placement and a tapered outline with a cel-shaded coat color.

Positioning the ear thickness and checking how the outline mirrors across the left/right sides so the outward bulge stays correct for both. I'm working through the ear's tilt direction so the tips lean up and slightly outward like a fox, then moving to eye placement on the skull surface using spherical coordinates.

For face markings, I'm keeping the coat cream with a dark nose, and adding red eyeliner streak decals near the outer corners of each eye using a simple curved SVG stroke, positioned using the same spherical hit-point approach as the eyes.

I should default dir explicitly for the eye decals since the default orientation is unclear, maybe using the hit normal for placement so the drawing orients correctly from different angles. Non-null assertions are fine here, and I still need to work out the skull surfaces from Part and get into the body paint setup with fur-edged coloring.

For the belly I'm layering a cel-shaded fur edge with a cream-to-tan gradient, letting the lighting handle shadow computation automatically. For the tail, I want a per-tail gradient from cream to gold rather than a fixed position, built along the catmull-rom path so each tail segment picks up color based on its position, then swept along the tail chain with smoothed radii.

Still writing sweep logic...

I'm placing decal markings on both sides of the tail near the middle, computing the frame orientation from the sweep path so the marks align with the tail's surface normal and tangent direction.

For the flame effect, I'm generating small rings at the tail tips and attaching card geometry with mixed blue and gold textures, varying size, rotation, and bend to create a flickering flame look that bends back toward the tail root.

For the hitodama orbs, I'm placing a small sphere core at each position with a pale blue glow, then attaching flame cards oriented upward and slightly offset below each orb using the same blue/gold texture mix at a smaller scale.

I'm working out symmetric left/right placements near the hip, head, and tail regions, checking they clear the tail geometry so the overall figure stays within a reasonable bounding height.

Now I'm deciding to scale down the tail lifts slightly for proportion, skipping eye glow, and adding flank swirl decals along with red leg markings.

I'm adding a gold orb-and-ring decal on the haunch and skipping front-leg red marks, then planning chest ruff scatter detailing near the neck mane cards.

Now I'm placing the skull part on the head bone with paint colors, then sweeping a tapered path from the muzzle base to tip with rounded caps to shape a flattened fox-like snout.

I'm sweeping the lower jaw separately with its own taper and bone, setting a jaw joint position relative to the head, then adding a small nose sphere with dark coloring and planning teeth and whisker placements along the head bone.

I'm orienting the ring and adding a hanging red spike tassel beneath it, then moving on to the necklace loop around the neck joint and planning bead placement along the chain.

Now I'm placing small gold sphere beads along that loop path and sweeping a thin gold strand through it, adjusting lift heights so the beads and sweep don't overlap oddly. I still need to add chest tufts and filter the neck ruff by position so it only covers the upper chest and neck region.

I'm working out the limb joint positions for both the front and hind legs on each side, choosing shoulder-to-paw and hip-to-paw coordinates with bend hints so the elbow sits back and the knee sits forward, matching natural fox leg posture, then naming each joint in the chain per side.

I'm adding muscle bulges at the shoulder joints and resolving how to reference the foot tip for claw placement, defaulting to the last joint index instead of relying on an uncertain `tip` property, while sketching out the paw ellipsoid position.

I need a tail base joint rooted off the hips with its own direction, feeding into the tail chain, and plan to loft the body surface across the spine and neck stations with a rounded start cap. Then I'll compute the tail point list using a lift factor and turn it all into code.
